 JUDGMENT
This appeal is filed by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 26.12.2019, passed by the Tribunal, in MVC No.2757/2017 seeking enhancement of compensation.

2. Heard the arguments and perused the material placed before the Court.
3.
The occurrence of accident, injuries sustained by the claimant, coverage of insurance are not in dispute in this case.
4. In the present case, from the medical evidence on record it is proved that the claimant had suffered the following injuries.
i) Fracture of shaft of humerus.
ii) Fracture of lateral condyle of left tibia.

The tribunal has awarded compensation under various heads as under:
 Sl. Heads.

Amount in  No. (Rs.)
 1. Towards pain and suffering.

20,000/-
 2. Towards medical expenses.

Towards loss of earning capacity 1,24,800/-
5.
Towards incidental expenses 1,800/-

2 like attendant charges, food etc.

Total: 1,64,751/-
6. Considering the nature of injuries sustained, compensation awarded by Tribunal is on lesser side.
Therefore, the same is required to be enhanced by modifying the judgment and award.

7. Considering the injuries sustained, a compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards pain and suffering,
Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities are awarded.
The compensation awarded towards medical expenses and hospital charges of Rs.18,151/- is as per the actual bills and receipts produced

;
therefore, the same is kept intact.

Further, Rs.9,000/- towards incidental expenses like food,
nourishment, traveling, attendant charges, etc., and NC: 2023:KHC-D:13229 Rs.30,750/- towards loss of income during laid up period for a period of three months, is awarded.
8. The doctor has stated that the claimant had suffered 50% of physical disability to the whole body.
Therefore, considering the evidence of the doctor, 17% functional disability is taken into consideration as the claimant had suffered two fractures as stated above.
9. The accident is caused in the year 2017.
Therefore, notional income of Rs.10,250/- per month is taken into consideration, which is recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The claimant was aged 46 years at the time of accident.
Therefore appropriate applicable multiplier is 13.

Hence, loss of future income due to disability is hereby reassessed and quantified as under:
Rs.10,250/- x 12 x 17/100 x 13 = Rs.2,71,830/-
10.

Thus, the claimant is entitled for total compensation under various heads as under:

Amount in No. (Rs.)
1. Towards injuries, pain and 30,000/- suffering.
2. Towards medical expenses.

3. Towards loss of income during 30,750/-
laid up period and medical treatment period.
5. Towards incidental charges like 9,000/- attendant charges, food, nourishment, conveyance, etc.,.
6. Towards loss of future earning 2,71,830/- capacity.
Total: 3,59,731/-
11.

Therefore, the claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,59,731/-, along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization, as against Rs.1,64,751/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

3 12.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.

ii) The judgment and award dated 26.12.2019 passed by the Senior Civil Judge NC:
2023:KHC-D:13229 and Addl. M.A.C.T, Bailhongal, in MVC No.2757/2017 stands modified.
iii) The claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,59,731/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
iv) The claimant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 124 days in filing the appeal.
v) The insurance company shall deposit the amount within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
vi) Send back the trial Court records along with a copy of this judgment.
vii) No order as to costs.
viii) Draw award accordingly.
